messages.subject: Distance 7.4 bug and incorrect estimates
parts:
Hello, 

I've just updated Distance 7.4 after learning of the bug. How do I check if my estimates using the old version are incorrect without redoing everything? I am to present new estimates of harbour porpoises in a few days and the estimates used MRDS and Cluster size, so I expect they are vulnerable to bug. 

Thanks!

Deanna

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: {Suspected Spam} [distance-sampling] Distance 7.4 bug and incorrect estimates
parts:
Greetings Deanna

Good idea to have a check of your previous analyses to determine if you need to re-run them.  There is more than one way to check your previous analyses, but perhaps the most straightforward would be to examine the survey properties of a former analysis.  Then check that the field names in the data correspond to the proper role they perform
In the screenshot, not the correspondence of field names and roles.  In Distance 7.4 Release 1, this correspondence was not correct when a new project was created.

A second check you could perform would be to re-run an analysis from Distance 7.4 Release 1 (assuming you still have Release 1 on your computer), but this time turn on the feature that echos the data sent to the MRDS engine (under Tools|Preferences):
with this option enabled, you can see what data are being sent to the MRDS engine in the Log window:
this will assist in detecting whether field names have gotten confused.  The user who posted the original bug found that the distance field and the size field contained identical information, leading to group size computations being incorrect.

Hope this is helpful, drop a note if you have more questions.
